plantvillage_0.description: Fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis.
plantvillage_0.treatment: At green-tip stage, apply Bacillus subtilis 5 g/L or Pseudomonas fluorescens 5 g/L. Chemical backup: Mancozeb 75% WP 2.5 g/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC 0.5 mL/L.
plantvillage_0.prevention: After leaf fall, spray 5% urea or Trichoderma viride 5 g/L on orchard-floor leaf litter. Prune interior branches to improve sunlight.
plantvillage_0.organic_option: 5% urea or Trichoderma viride 5 g/L on fallen leaves.
plantvillage_0.bio_fungicide: Bacillus subtilis 5 g/L; Pseudomonas fluorescens 5 g/L.
plantvillage_0.chemical_option: Mancozeb 75% WP 2.5 g/L; Difenoconazole 25% EC 0.5 mL/L.
plantvillage_0.field_sanitation: Decompose/remove overwintering leaf litter and prune dense interior branches.
plantvillage_0.weather_condition: Favorable weather for fungal development requires preventive management.
plantvillage_0.humidity_risk: High humidity/favorable wet conditions increase scab risk.
plantvillage_0.regional_advice: India context; follow local ICAR/CIBRC and product-label guidance.
plantvillage_0.safety_note: Use biological and chemical products according to the registered product label and local agricultural guidance. Do not tank-mix bio-fungicides directly with synthetic fungicides; the source recommends a 5–7 day gap.
plantvillage_0.source: crop_disease_prevention_guide(3).pdf — ICAR-Aligned Crop Disease Prevention & IDM Guide (India Context)

plantvillage_34.description: Target spot caused by Corynespora cassiicola.
plantvillage_34.treatment: Spray Trichoderma viride 5 g/L. Chemical options: Zineb 75% WP 2 g/L or Pyraclostrobin 20% WG 1 g/L.
plantvillage_34.prevention: Use bamboo staking and prune lower leaves up to approximately 30 cm.
plantvillage_34.chemical_option: Zineb 75% WP 2 g/L; Pyraclostrobin 20% WG 1 g/L.
plantvillage_34.field_sanitation: Prune lower foliage and improve crop airflow.

plantvillage_35.description: Viral disease transmitted by whitefly vectors.
plantvillage_35.treatment: Control whiteflies using Beauveria bassiana 5 mL/L. Chemical vector-control options listed by the source include Imidacloprid 17.8% SL 0.5 mL/L or Cyantraniliprole 10.26% OD 1.8 mL/L.
plantvillage_35.prevention: Raise nursery under 60-mesh nets, install 20 yellow sticky traps/acre, and rogue infected plants immediately.
plantvillage_35.chemical_option: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL 0.5 mL/L; Cyantraniliprole 10.26% OD 1.8 mL/L.

plantvillage_36.prevention: Raise nursery under 60-mesh nets, use sanitation, and avoid mechanical spread.
plantvillage_36.bio_pesticide: Beauveria bassiana 5 mL/L is listed for whitefly-vector management in the virus-management section.
plantvillage_36.chemical_option: The source lists Imidacloprid/Cyantraniliprole for vector control.
plantvillage_36.field_sanitation: Rogue infected plants and maintain clean nursery/tools.

irrigation_advice: Maintain appropriate irrigation according to crop growth stage.

rice_0.description: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae.
treatment: Treat seeds with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed.
Dip seedling roots in Pseudomonas fluorescens slurry @ 20 g/L for 30 minutes before transplanting.
At initial symptom appearance, spray Streptocycline @ 0.15 g/L + Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L.
prevention: Avoid clipping root or leaf tips of seedlings during transplanting.
Drain excess water from the field for 2–3 days during early tillering.
Avoid excessive nitrogen application (>120 kg N/ha).
organic_option: Pseudomonas fluorescens seed treatment @ 10 g/kg seed.
Pseudomonas fluorescens root dip @ 20 g/L for 30 minutes.
chemical_option: Streptocycline @ 0.15 g/L + Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L at initial symptom appearance.
irrigation_advice: Drain excess field water for 2–3 days during early tillering.
fertilizer_advice: Avoid excessive nitrogen application above 120 kg N/ha.
rice_0.safety_note: Follow product labels and local agricultural recommendations when using chemical products.

rice_1.description: Rice brown spot caused by Bipolaris oryzae / Helminthosporium oryzae.
treatment: Treat seeds with Trichoderma viride @ 10 g/kg seed.
Alternatively treat seeds with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed.
Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L at maximum tillering.
Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 mL/L.
prevention: Correct soil nutrient deficiencies, especially Potassium, Silicon and Zinc.
organic_option: Trichoderma viride seed treatment @ 10 g/kg seed.
Pseudomonas fluorescens seed treatment @ 10 g/kg seed.
irrigation_advice: Avoid water stress during tillering.
rice_1.safety_note: Follow product labels and local agricultural recommendations.

rice_2.description: No rice disease detected by the Rice V2 model.
prevention: Maintain balanced irrigation and nutrient management.
Inspect leaves regularly for early disease symptoms.
irrigation_advice: Maintain appropriate field moisture according to crop growth stage.
field_sanitation: Keep the field and surrounding area free from unnecessary plant debris.

rice_3.description: Rice blast caused by Magnaporthe oryzae / Pyricularia oryzae.
treatment: Treat seeds with Trichoderma harzianum @ 10 g/kg seed.
Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L preventively before tillering and panicle initiation.
Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 mL/L.
prevention: Split nitrogen application into 3–4 equal doses instead of heavy basal application.
Keep bunds free of weed hosts.
organic_option: Trichoderma harzianum seed treatment @ 10 g/kg seed.
irrigation_advice: Avoid late-night overhead irrigation.
fertilizer_advice: Split nitrogen application into 3–4 equal doses.
field_sanitation: Keep bunds free of weed hosts.
rice_3.safety_note: Follow product labels and local agricultural recommendations.

rice_4.description: Rice leaf scald caused by Microdochium oryzae / Rhynchosporium oryzae.
treatment: Spray Bacillus subtilis @ 5 g/L at initial leaf-tip scalding appearance.
Alternatively spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L.
Apply Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L or Benomyl 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L.
prevention: Maintain optimal plant density of 20 cm × 15 cm.
Maintain good light penetration and airflow.
weather_condition: Good airflow and light penetration are recommended through proper plant spacing.
rice_4.safety_note: Follow product labels and local agricultural recommendations.

rice_5.description: Rice sheath blight caused by Rhizoctonia solani.
treatment: Enrich 100 kg FYM with 2.5 kg Trichoderma harzianum, incubate for 7 days and apply during field preparation.
Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L toward the base of plants at tillering.
Spray Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 2.0 mL/L or Validamycin 3% L @ 2.0 mL/L directed at the canopy base.
prevention: Destroy previous crop stubble to eliminate sclerotia.
Apply Potassium in two split doses.
bio_fungicide: Trichoderma harzianum @ 2.5 kg per 100 kg FYM.
fertilizer_advice: Apply Potassium in two split doses.
field_sanitation: Clean field bunds.
Destroy previous crop stubble to eliminate sclerotia.
rice_5.safety_note: Follow product labels and local agricultural recommendations.

prevention: Avoid excessive overhead irrigation during grain filling and dough stages.

Pseudomonas fluorescens seed treatment at 10 g/kg seed.
bio_fungicide: Trichoderma viride 1% WP at 10 g/kg seed.
chemical_option: Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L under wet weather conditions during heading.
Propiconazole 25% EC at 1.0 mL/L during flowering/heading.
irrigation_advice: Avoid excessive overhead irrigation during grain filling and dough stages.
weather_condition: Wet and humid conditions can increase risk.
wheat_0.safety_note: Follow the product label and local agricultural recommendations when using chemical fungicides.

bio_fungicide: Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg/acre enriched in 100 kg FYM.
